key_insight: Partitioning Pauli strings with an F₂-linear hash replaces global deduplication synchronization with independent gate-application tasks requiring bounded communication.
engineering_relevance: The approach pools memory across cores and compute nodes to scale memory-bound quantum simulation beyond single-node capacity.
method: Evolve observables as sparse sums of Pauli strings in the Heisenberg picture.
Assign strings to partitions using an F₂-linear hash.
Exploit the guarantee that a k-qubit channel couples each partition to at most 4^k gate-determined partitions.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks of the open-source implementation report efficient within-node and cross-node scaling, simulations exceeding 10^11 Pauli strings, and longer accessible many-body evolution times.
watch_item: The 4^k coupling bound grows exponentially with channel size, so communication costs may become substantial for channels acting on many qubits.
